title: Span
tagline: Call Span. Ask if you’ll make payroll. Watch the answer get made.

sections.inspiration: Small business owners make money decisions every day with no answer. 'Can I pay my people Friday?' lives in their books, spread across the bank balance, forty unpaid invoices, each customer's habits, and the bills due. Turning that into a yes or a no has always needed an accountant they can't afford, slower than they can wait. Intuit's challenge text named it: work that used to be too slow or costly to run. We wanted the owner to be able to ask out loud and watch the answer get made.
sections.what_it_does: Span is a cash assistant you talk to. Call it in the browser or type, and ask 'am I making payroll Friday?' While it works, a web page draws its reasoning live as a workflow: pulling context, scoring every open invoice by that customer's payment history, forecasting cash on payday, the answer, the levers that close the gap, and the ask. Say yes and it texts the right customers, handles their replies, negotiates installments with the customer's agent under your rules, takes the payment through a pay link, and the gap on screen ticks down. At the end it generates a one-page report. Second question it handles: 'should I take this customer's order?'
sections.how_we_built_it: Data: Intuit's 100-company QuickBooks dataset flattened into Tiger Postgres (84k invoices, 144k payments, 26k payroll runs). Fast lane: a payment-behavior model (gradient-boosted trees, trained across all companies, last 60 days held out) predicts when each invoice pays and whether it ever will; Jev fills this role where available. Slow lane: Gemini plans, decides levers, writes the spoken answer, and writes the report. Reminders are drafted by a template drafter grounded in the invoice and the customer's payment history, and every message is a labeled simulated channel until a real sender is configured. Every tool call is an event on a server-sent stream; the frontend (designed and built in Paper) renders those events as a workflow canvas with six node types. Photon (a Spectrum iMessage line) sends the reminders as real iMessages to the demo phone; customer replies come from the simulated customer agents, labeled as such. Voice runs in the browser. Fetch uAgents run the simulated customer agents; a local bureau negotiates installments with Span’s agent. Pay links use a simulated card, labeled as such on the pay page. We traced the payroll run with the Sentry SDK locally; that trace is how we caught the bug below. Devin built the loader and the pay page. Runs locally (Postgres + TimescaleDB in Docker); the project site is youare.cooking.
sections.company_challenges: Intuit: real-time analysis on the provided dataset, answering a question QuickBooks users can't get today. Fetch.ai: uAgents run agent-to-agent negotiation between Span and each customer’s agent. Photon: reminders go out as real iMessages over a Spectrum line. Paper: the workflow canvas is the interface, designed in Paper. Cognition: Devin built two modules (session links attached). Sentry: a local SDK trace of the payroll run caught the forecast bug; write-up below. MLH: Gemini, Tiger Data, ElevenLabs; domain youare.cooking (.cooking, a GoDaddy Registry TLD) is the project site. Model Learning track: learned payment-behavior model with held-out metrics.
sections.challenges: The demo had to be honest, not scripted. Three hard parts. First, the forecast had to be right: our first cash rollup silently dropped overdue bills, which flipped Palletbay's answer from 'short $385' to 'fine' — caught on a Sentry trace of the payroll run and fixed with a reconciled-total regression test. Second, real time: scoring 204 invoices can't block a spoken answer, so the run streams events as it works — the frontend replays them into the canvas and the report is rebuilt from the same stream, which kept UI, voice and document from ever disagreeing. Third, negotiation under owner rules: the customer-side agents only exist at demo time, so we generated their behavior from each customer's real payment history in the dataset and kept every round on the event stream so it could be audited.
sections.accomplishments: A full loop that actually closes: question -> live reasoning workflow -> spoken answer -> 'yes' -> reminders out -> reply -> agent-to-agent negotiation under owner rules -> real payment rail -> gap ticking down -> one-page report. The fast lane is a model we trained, not an LLM guess: MAE 1.25 days and 0.968 AUC on held-out invoices across 86 companies. The whole demo is deterministic and recordable — one npm command produces the video, stills and thumbnail — and every number on screen traces back to dataset rows, which is what lets us say 'no' on stage with a straight face.
sections.what_we_learned: Reasoning-on-display changes what the product is: owners don't trust 'the model says no,' they trust seeing their own invoices scored. We also learned the dataset fights back — payroll cadence, partial payments and overdue bills each broke a naive rollup before we reconciled against invoice_facts. And events-first architecture paid for itself three times: live canvas, deterministic replay for the demo video, and the generated report all consume the exact same stream.
sections.whats_next: Real telephony end to end (Gemini Live + ElevenLabs over Photon media streams, Twilio fallback), a fine-tuned reminder drafter, the Agentverse registration so ASI:One discovers the agent on its own, and write-side rails: posting payments and deferrals back into QuickBooks via Intuit's API instead of the pay-link ledger.
sections.built_with: python, fastapi, postgresql, tigerdata, gemini, openrouter, scikit-learn, uagents, fetch.ai, photon, elevenlabs, sentry, devin, paper
sections.disclosures: Customer agents in the demo are simulated from each customer's real payment history in the dataset. No dataset rows were modified.

sentry_bug_writeup.status: verified with local Sentry SDK trace; cloud upload pending DSN
sentry_bug_writeup.bug: Cash forecast excluded overdue unpaid bills by filtering due dates BETWEEN as_of and target.
sentry_bug_writeup.impact: Palletbay omitted four overdue liabilities totaling $1,598.55. The two-week expected payroll gap was incorrectly $0; corrected gap is $384.94.
sentry_bug_writeup.fix: Include unpaid bills issued by dataset as_of and due on or before target. A regression test checks the reconciled total of $10,866.86.
